page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-224 is an enterprise-scale, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for massive memory-bound workloads, the instance provides 224 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 5,952 GB of system RAM. This configuration yields a memory allocation ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per virtual core, accommodating working sets that far exceed standard memory profiles.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this configuration, and the instance includes no local storage volumes. Storage must be provisioned via remote block storage networks, aligning the platform toward architectures that decouple persistent data volumes from compute and memory. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are also not bundled with the server.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server targets maximum resource density within system memory. In-memory databases, large-scale analytics engines, enterprise resource planning suites, and extensive caching architectures that require continuous multi-terabyte memory retention operate efficiently on this instance without paging bottlenecks.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-224 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance configured with 224 dedicated vCPUs and 5,952 GB of RAM, delivering an expansive 26.57 GB of memory per virtual core. Tailored for enterprise workloads requiring vast memory retention, the instance features no integrated GPU hardware and provides no local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data needs. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The heavy skew toward memory over compute makes the server structurally cost-efficient for platforms whose operations are strictly constrained by RAM capacity rather than raw compute scaling. As a result, the instance is well matched for large in-memory databases, memory-resident data caches, business enterprise software, and real-time operational data processing environments.
